Now, she's been calling and texting me, demanding to know where it is and saying things like, "I got it for you, I can touch it whenever I want." My mom helped me get it, but that doesn't automatically give her the right to handle it whenever she wants, especially if I've explicitly stated that I don't want that to happen. On the other hand, my mom did help me get the flute. She signed the contract and managed the payments, which was necessary because I was only 17 at the time and couldn't sign the contract myself. She might feel that her involvement gives her some ownership or at least the right to interact with the flute. However, I paid off the entire amount myself, so the flute is now solely mine. Another angle to consider is the emotional aspect. My mom and I don't have a great relationship, and since I moved in with my boyfriend, things have improved a bit, but not entirely. This situation might be exacerbating any existing tensions between us. She might be taking my refusal personally, feeling that I'm not respecting her or acknowledging her help in getting the flute for me. But from my perspective, I need to protect my flute. It's not just an instrument; it's a significant investment, both financially and emotionally. I've worked hard to pay it off, and I want to ensure it's taken care of properly. Allowing someone else to touch it, especially if they don't have the same level of care and attention, could potentially damage it. Moreover, setting boundaries is important in any relationship, including the one with my mom. If I don't establish clear boundaries, it could lead to more conflicts in the future. It's okay to say no when something is important to me, especially when it comes to my personal belongings. However, I also need to consider how I communicate this boundary. Being firm is one thing, but being respectful and understanding is another. Maybe I can explain to her why the flute is so important to me and why I don't want her to touch it. In summary, while it's understandable that my mom feels entitled to touch the flute because she helped me get it, the flute is now mine, and I have the right to set boundaries regarding its handling.
